guide_line: Convert units with factors, and convert temperatures among °C, K, and °F.
steps: Write a conversion factor as a ratio that equals one, then multiply so the unit you have cancels.
Use these OpenStax AF2e Table 1.6 factors: 1 in = 2.54 cm (exact), 1 lb = 453.59 g, 1 oz = 28.349 g, 1 km = 0.62137 mi, 1 mi = 1609.3 m, 1 qt = 0.94635 L, 1 tbsp = 14.787 mL, and 1 m = 1.0936 yd.
Round a multiplication or division result to four significant figures when the measured value has four. An exact factor does not limit the result.
Kelvin and Celsius share the size of one degree: K = °C + 273.15, and °C = K − 273.15. Keep the hundredths place.
Fahrenheit does not share that zero. °F = (9/5) × °C + 32, and °C = (5/9) × (°F − 32).

worked_example.q: Convert 6.000 in to centimeters. Use 1 in = 2.54 cm, exact.
steps: Multiply by 2.54 cm / 1 in so inches cancel.
6.000 × 2.54 = 15.24. The 2.54 is exact, so the four figures in 6.000 remain: 15.24 cm.

similar_problem.q: Convert 3.000 in to centimeters. Use 1 in = 2.54 cm, exact.
similar_problem.hint: Multiply 3.000 by 2.54 cm per inch. Because 2.54 is exact, keep four figures.

problems.q: Convert 18.00 in to centimeters. Use 1 in = 2.54 cm, exact.
problems.why: 18.00 in × 2.54 cm/in = 45.72 cm. The factor is exact, so the four figures in 18.00 stay.
hints: Cancel inches with 2.54 cm per inch. Do not round away a figure, because 2.54 is exact.

problems.q: Convert 2.000 lb to grams. Use 1 lb = 453.59 g.
problems.why: 2.000 lb × 453.59 g/lb = 907.18 g. Four significant figures give 907.2 g.
hints: Multiply 2.000 by 453.59 g per pound, then keep four significant figures.

problems.q: Convert 75.00 g to ounces. Use 1 oz = 28.349 g.
hints: Divide 75.00 g by 28.349 g per ounce, then keep four significant figures.

problems.q: Convert 12.00 km to miles. Use 1 km = 0.62137 mi.
problems.why: 12.00 km × 0.62137 mi/km = 7.45644 mi, which rounds to 7.456 mi.
hints: Multiply 12.00 km by 0.62137 miles per kilometer.

problems.q: Convert 2.500 qt to liters. Use 1 qt = 0.94635 L.
problems.why: 2.500 qt × 0.94635 L/qt = 2.365875 L, which rounds to 2.366 L.
hints: Multiply 2.500 quarts by 0.94635 liters per quart.

problems.q: Convert 1.200 mi to meters. Use 1 mi = 1609.3 m.
problems.why: 1.200 mi × 1609.3 m/mi = 1931.16 m. Four significant figures give 1.931 × 10^3 m.
hints: Multiply 1.200 miles by 1609.3 meters per mile, and show four figures in scientific notation.

problems.q: Convert 1.500 qt to milliliters. Use 1 qt = 0.94635 L and 1 L = 1000 mL.
problems.why: 1.500 qt × 0.94635 L/qt × 1000 mL/L = 1419.525 mL. The first dropped digit is 5 and nonzero digits follow, so four figures give 1.420 × 10^3 mL.
hints: Change quarts to liters with 0.94635, then use 1000 mL in each liter.

problems.q: A 3.600 lb sample of liquid fills 1.800 qt. What is the density in g/mL? Use 1 lb = 453.59 g, 1 qt = 0.94635 L, and 1 L = 1000 mL.
hints: Change pounds to grams and quarts to milliliters, then divide the gram mass by the milliliter volume.

problems.why: K = °C + 273.15 = 25.00 + 273.15 = 298.15 K. Both temperatures have hundredths, so the sum keeps hundredths.
hints: Add 273.15 to 25.00. Keep two digits after the decimal.
Subtract 273.15 from 310.15. Both values already show hundredths.
Multiply 20.00 by 9/5, then add 32. Keep the hundredths.
Subtract 32 from 98.60 first, then multiply that difference by 5/9.
A temperature below zero still uses the same addition: add 273.15 to −10.00.
Change 50.00 °F into Celsius first with (5/9) times (50.00 minus 32). Then add 273.15.

problems.q: Convert 3.000 tbsp to milliliters. Use 1 tbsp = 14.787 mL.
problems.why: 3.000 tbsp × 14.787 mL/tbsp = 44.361 mL, which rounds to 44.36 mL.
hints: Multiply 3.000 by 14.787 mL per tablespoon, then keep four significant figures.

problems.q: Convert 5.000 m to yards. Use 1 m = 1.0936 yd.
problems.why: 5.000 m × 1.0936 yd/m = 5.468 yd. Both the measurement and the rounded product have four figures.
hints: Multiply 5.000 meters by 1.0936 yards per meter.
